title: Vance says he was told Huang was not under investigation | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that federal officials told him reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation, downplaying concerns that Huang’s reported affair with a womansuspected of having ties to Chinese intelligencecould pose a national security risk.

“We were told that he was under no investigation,” Vance told CNN’s Kit Maher at a pre-Thanksgiving meal for US troops in Dayton, Ohio. “We received the assurances that he was not under any significant – he was under no investigation, and the accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence.”

Vance is the latest administration official topublicly defend Huangand reject the suggestion that he and his company were implicated in any wrongdoing. On Tuesday, when Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked whether Huang had been investigated, he responded, “For what?”

Vance said Blanche was among “multiple people” in the United States government who had given him assurances about Huang.

“I talked to the attorney general. I talked to other folks as well,” he said. “I just don’t think that people should lose their jobs because anonymous sources accuse them of things in The New York Times when those things actually aren’t rooted in real evidence.”

President Donald Trump has similarly defended Huang in public, and sources said he tapped Vance to help get Huang reinstated to Nvidia after he was ousted amid reports of his extramarital affairs.

Huang has been under intense scrutiny since late last month, whenThe New York Times first reportedon his close connection to a woman named Alice Huang, an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed who was suspected of also being tied to Chinese intelligence. That scrutiny intensified when it was revealed Jensen Huang and Alice Huang were in a romantic relationship. The two are not related.

But exactly what steps the US government has taken to assess the possible intelligence risk and explore any possible criminal wrongdoing have long been murky. And even if Jensen Huang was not the direct target of an investigation, that does not mean his activities did not draw scrutiny.

The Department of Commerce began a probe into Megaspeed in 2024 and conducted an on-site check with Singaporean law enforcement in June 2025, during which it interviewedAlice Huang, whom it identified as the company CEO. The probe scrutinized whether Megaspeed, a customer of Nvidia, diverted highly coveted US semiconductors to entities in China in violation of US export controls.

The Justice Department has since taken on the lead role in the criminal investigation into Megaspeed.

The US intelligence community has also been exploring the extent to which Alice Huang was connected to the Chinese government, though multiple sources told CNN earlier this month that the intelligence collected on her did not conclusively prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.

Trump told CNBC on Monday, “We’ve done a very thorough investigation, and the investigation showed that [Jensen Huang] did, I mean, he had bad judgment having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong.” But pressed about what exactly US investigations had found, Blanche was evasive just a day later.

“The FBI, law enforcement, looks into things all the time. That doesn’t necessarily become a criminal investigation. Doesn’t necessarily become an indictment. It just literally is that it’s looking into things,” he said.

Jensen Huang is still facing scrutiny –especially on Capitol Hill, where he is set to testify publicly and behind closed doors next week.

Officials told congressional staff in an in-depth briefing on Nvidia on Tuesday that US intelligence believes that Alice Huang was introduced to an officer with China’s Ministry of State Security via a mutual friend last year. The officials said the officer is a public-facing official who works in an office within the Ministry of State Security that overtly interacts with a range of major companies that operate in China, according to a person familiar with the briefing.

When pressed by the staffers about whether Alice Huang was spying on Nvidia for the Ministry of State Security – or tasked with doing so – officials did not indicate that they had any intelligence suggesting that Huang was proactively providing sensitive information about Nvidia to the Chinese officer, that source said.

The Ministry of State Security has been spying on Alice Huang, sources previously told CNN. And a source familiar with the recent congressional briefing said the administration did say that a man thought to be Alice Huang’s husband was believed to be a Chinese asset and had regular contact with the Ministry of State Security.

Trump on Tuesday encouraged Jensen Huang to tell the truth in his upcoming appearances and indicated he would be open to pardoning the CEO.

“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post.

Asked whether Huang would need a pardon, Vance similarly said, “I don’t think he needs a pardon at all.”

Vance said the decision to reinstate Huang at his company was ultimately made by Nvidia’s board, and he did not detail his reported role in the matter.

The vice president called Nvidia’s chips central to the United States’ effort to stay ahead of China in the AI race and said the administration sees Huang’s return as a chance for the company to focus on following American export controls.

“We really do care about ensuring those chips do not fall into the wrong hands,” Vance said. “We expect that Nvidia will be a partner in that moving forward and in complying with American export controls.”
